formula: cbind(NumYes, NumNo) ~ factor(ContCntr) + I(1000 * TargCntr) + (0 + I(1000 * TargCntr) | Obs) + (1 + I(1000 * TargCntr) | Obs:ContCntr)
notes: Read MPDiR inst/scripts/Ch9.R (Knoblauch and Maloney 2012, ch. 9, mixed-effects models): with TrgCnt1000 = 1000 * TargCntr and FCtxCnt = factor(ContCntr), Context.glmm1 to Context.glmm3b compare random structures by anova and the final Context.glmm4 <- glmer(cbind(NumYes, NumNo) ~ FCtxCnt + TrgCnt1000 + (TrgCnt1000 + 0 | Obs) + (TrgCnt1000 | Obs:FCtxCnt), family = binomial('probit')). Six observers, four flanker contrasts, five target contrasts. Hand check #162: a binomial probit is outside Family, so family is blank (read.md). Successes stored beside their failures without a trials column stay count, as faraway soybean (every row holds 24 trials), NumNo ignored, against the outside check's binomial. The by-observer term is a slope without an intercept, filed TargCntr||Obs, the nearest form, since the contract gives every grouping factor an intercept; the formula states 0 +. Context.glmm1 to Context.glmm3b have the same response and grouping, so they file no row.

formula: values ~ cond * factor(time) + (1 | rat) + (1 | rat:cond), compound-symmetric residual correlation within rat:cond
notes: The page describes the design and fits no model: both soleus muscles of seven rats, one randomized to pinacidil and one to placebo, contraction force measured every 30 seconds on 15 occasions (Kristensen and Hansen 2004, a tutorial on repeated measures). M1 takes rat and muscle (rat:cond) intercepts and time as a factor. values are normalized to the first time point, so time 0 is 100 for every muscle. Hand check #162: Kristensen and Hansen's SAS appendix (2004) fits M1, the repeated-measurements ANOVA, by proc mixed (MIVQUE0) on all 15 time points: model Y = Treatment Time Treatment*Time, random Animal Animal*Treatment and repeated/type=CS subject=Animal*Treatment, so the row is yes; the compound-symmetric residual adds the exchangeable correlation within a muscle that the rat:cond intercept also gives, named in the formula. M2 and M4 are models 2 and 3; the cubic random-coefficient regression under Other Possible Models is not fitted. 7 rats of two muscles, 15 rows each.

formula: log(values) ~ cond * factor(time) + (1 | rat), first-order autoregressive residual correlation within rat:cond
notes: Hand check #162: model 2 from the outside check. Kristensen and Hansen's SAS appendix (2004) fits M2, the linear mixed-effects model on log(values), by proc mixed (ML): model logY = Treatment Time Treatment*Time, random Animal and repeated/type=AR(1) subject=Animal*Treatment, after deleting the even time points, so it fits times 1, 3, ..., 13; the row stands on the whole table, the subset here. The muscle enters only through the autoregressive residual, so rat is the one grouping factor. values are normalized to 100 at time 0.

formula: values ~ A*exp(B*time) + C; A ~ cond; B ~ cond + (1 | rat:cond); C ~ cond + (1 | rat:cond); Gaussian, nl=TRUE
notes: Hand check #162: model 3 from the outside check. Kristensen and Hansen's SAS appendix (2004) fits M4, the nonlinear mixed-effects model of their Eq. 6, by proc nlmixed: pred = (mu1 + a1*Treat)*exp((mu2 + a2*Treat + u2)*Time) + mu3 + a3*Treat + u3, u2 and u3 normal with subject=Animal_ID, one id per muscle. Their covariance is not significant and is removed before the treatment tests (Table 5), so the row states that final model, independent muscle effects on the decay B and the asymptote C; the first fit with the covariance has the same response and grouping and files no row. A has no random effect, since A + C is the relative force at time 0. rat is unused, the muscle being rat:cond; time is numeric, 0 to 14 at 30 s.

CD4 holds the square-rooted count. Hand check #162: Guo and Carlin's equation (5) regresses the square-root CD4 count on time, time by drug, gender, previous opportunistic infection and stratum, with a correlated patient intercept and slope (PROC MIXED, type=un), this row. drug enters only through obstime:drug and stays among the covariates by the row grammar, against the outside check. Models III to VI of their Table 2, with patient intercepts only, have the same response and grouping, so they file no row. time and death are the survival outcome.
